Subject: Marketplace access fee & routing term exception request — NexusCloud (AWS Private Offer)

Team,

Quick summary: NexusCloud is a reseller partner for a mid-size retail customer and wants an AWS private offer listing that routes revenue through the marketplace with a nonstandard routing split. Specifically: Nexus is asking for a temporary waiver of the AWS one-time "market access" fee and for the revenue routing to credit their reseller commission bucket (vs. Redwood recognizing 100% and paying downstream). The ARR is small (~$180k first 12 months) but this is strategic for the reseller channel in retail.

Why ask execs: deal desk flagged this as nonstandard because it touches AWS listing/access credit and changes our normal rev routing, which could affect revenue recognition and partner commissions. Karthik, can you confirm deal desk risk + recommended mitigation? Marissa, we need an approval memo we can send to AWS and Nexus if we get signoff.

Attachments: AWS_Terms_Ask_v1.pdf (redlined ask from Nexus)

Next steps requested:
- Deal desk: short risk summary + fallback if AWS denies waiver
- Sales: exec approval for either (A) one-time access fee waiver + allow Nexus routing for 12 months OR (B) deny waiver and keep standard routing; if A, then authorize special commission split 10% to Nexus for 12 months

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Sales — Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
[attachment: AWS_Terms_Ask_v1.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace access fee & routing term exception request — NexusCloud (AWS Private Offer)

Laura / Marissa —

Thanks for the context. Deal desk review notes below:

1) Accounting / revenue recognition: Allowing revenue to route directly to a reseller bucket changes when Redwood recognizes revenue if we accept AWS routing for the private offer. We need to ensure contracts reflect that Redwood is still the seller of record or that the reseller arrangement includes clear pass-through language.
2) Marketplace economics: Typically AWS charges a 6% marketplace fee; waiver requests are allowed but are rare. If AWS waives listing fees, they will want some offset (e.g., promotional credits or a minimum commit).
3) Commissions: Our standard reseller commission is 15% of net-recognized revenue. Nexus is asking for a 10% special split (i.e., Redwood would reduce our take, or we accept routing that causes Nexus to receive funds directly).
4) Risk mitigation: Require a short SOW addendum specifying the 12-month term, clawback if customer churns inside 90 days, and legal signoff on pass-through wording. Also request AWS provide written confirmation of any fee waiver and routing mechanics.

Recommendation (deal desk): escalate to execs for a one-time exception with the following guardrails:
- Limit to 12 months and $200k ARR cap
- Clawback for early termination (90 days)
- Legal must approve pass-through wording prior to DocuSign
- Redwood to own support and liability for the customer experience

Attaching a brief risk memo and proposed guardrails. If execs are OK, I will draft the redlined DocuSign payload.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk

Subject: Re: Marketplace access fee & routing term exception request — NexusCloud (AWS Private Offer)

Hi Laura / team,

Appreciate the detailed ask and the guardrails. AWS can be flexible on the one-time listing fee in limited cases where there is a clear channel motion and a short-term runway to convert. Our proposed approach:

- We can waive the one-time market access fee for the initial listing provided Redwood commits to 
  a) either a 12-month listing promotion (AWS credits applied to the listing) OR b) a minimum of $150k billed through the marketplace in the first 12 months.
- Revenue routing: AWS supports marking the transaction to credit NexusCloud as reseller, but AWS will require a reseller agreement signature and evidence of the reseller relationship.
- Marketplace fee: standard AWS marketplace fee (6%) still applies to gross. Any special commission split between Redwood and Nexus must be handled at the contractual level between Redwood and Nexus (AWS will not arbitrate internal split).

Attached is AWS_Terms_Response_v2.pdf with technical routing requirements. If Redwood accepts, AWS will issue the private offer once the reseller agreement is in place and DocuSign payload is finalized.

Best,
Anna Carroll
Partner Sales, AWS Marketplace
[attachment: AWS_Terms_Response_v2.pdf]

Subject: Re: Marketplace access fee & routing term exception request — NexusCloud (AWS Private Offer)

Folks —

Executive decision: APPROVED (one-time exception with guardrails). Summary of final terms we will accept and instruct legal to formalize:

1) AWS will provide listing credit (waive one-time access fee) conditioned on either $150k billed or 12-month promotional credit schedule per Anna's note.
2) Redwood authorizes a special reseller commission routing to NexusCloud for the first 12 months: Nexus receives 10% commission on net recognized revenue; Redwood will record revenue consistent with pass-through wording reviewed by legal.
3) Guardrails: 12-month limit, $200k ARR cap (whichever triggers first), 90-day clawback on early termination, legal signoff required on pass-through clause and on the DocuSign payload.
4) Redwood to own support and warranty for the customer; Nexus to handle first-line procurement relationship.

Karthik — please create the DocuSign package with the clauses and the clawback language and circulate for countersignature. Neha / Marissa — coordinate partner onboarding and PR credits. Anna — please confirm AWS will issue the private offer once we upload the reseller agreement and DocuSign is complete.

I'll follow up with a one-page exec memo for our finance and accounting teams.

Thanks everyone —
Laura
